title: Source-of-income and voucher protection
requirement: A housing provider may not refuse to rent, apply different terms, or advertise a preference based on an applicant’s source of income, including Housing Choice vouchers, public assistance, SSI, or wages.
coverage_conditions: Housing providers covered by FEHA, including landlords, real estate agents, tenant screening companies, and public housing authorities in California.
exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants on protected characteristics, but still may not publish discriminatory statements or ads.
penalty: Remedies include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to the housing denied, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.
citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act: source of income discrimination
quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

title: Criminal-history screening limits
requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice matters, and may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories; a denial must be directly related to tenant ability and safety.
coverage_conditions: Housing providers and tenant screening companies screening applicants in California, whether done directly or by a third party.
citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act: criminal history screening
quoted_span: Generally, a housing provider may check the criminal history of an applicant, but there are some limitations. Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.

note: Complaint deadlines and agency jurisdiction only; no rules in the six categories.

title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade, or coerce another person to adopt a price or commercial term the algorithm recommends.
coverage_conditions: Any person using or distributing a methodology that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or influence prices or commercial terms; end consumers excluded.
penalty: Violation is punishable as a crime under the Cartwright Act.
quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
interaction: Nothing in the section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
